name: Zoe Nash
life: “I still remember phoning a brother who only asked about the weather.” On Thursday, near the bank steps, Zoe takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I chose the brother who hears my ordinary complaints and never asks for an exciting case.
appearance: Off duty, look for an old plum windbreaker and a printed handkerchief folded into the pocket. Zoe has a long face and high cheekbones, with short, uneven waves that refuse to lie flat. Zoe presses the lips together to keep a smile in during a conversation.
personality: Zoe thinks best while walking. Sitting beneath someone's office clock makes Zoe sound more certain than they feel, an effect close friends have learned to distrust.
agenda: To give the brother one ordinary story from home.
family: Jay Knight is Zoe’s cousin raised in the same household. A parcel came home years late with the handwriting still recognizable. Since then nobody in the family opens a hard letter alone unless they specifically ask to. Zoe stays for the silence after the call. Asked about *The waiting-room plant*, Jay says, “I know it by the smell on my fingers after my daughter's surgery.”
connections: Oakley Roman. The sign painter asks how the brother who listens would want his name spelled.
